concepts.credibleEnvelope: Simulation-credible only on empty/low-traffic pistes with written permission, rider 7–16 m/s, head/cross/calm wind 0–9 m/s (tailwind ≥6 m/s → 39–80 %), and only if: canopy L/D ≥≈0.7 with ≥50 % reefed-glide retention, a boom gimbal that holds ≤0.5° pointing under ≈0.4–1 N·m, a heave-comp winch with ≤30 ms lag at 6–8 m/s, a 45° trumpet dock, and a custom 60° 4K optic — and if a permanent few-pixel boom stub over the rider is accepted as footage.
concepts.auditVerdict: Reproduces exactly (39/39) and passes all 13 judged metrics as modelled with the developer-tolerant artefact rule (avail 81.5 %, jitter p90 1.66, setup 4.7 s, ops 1, F 28.1 N, KE 12.9 J, headClear 1.105 m, endurance 56.9 min). Safety metrics are now robust; footage availability is knife-edge (≤1.5 pp margin, fails at L/D 0.6, mass +15 %, or a strict ≥1 px artefact rule) and rests on two idealised actuators (zero-lag heave winch beyond its own motor model; a gimbal driving a 1.2 m boom with motors too small for its simulated torque). The clothesline hazard is unfixed by design. Verdict: conditional pass as a research concept; not a usable product until tow/bench tests settle polar, gimbal, winch and dock.

US: Part 107/recreational rules require VLOS by the operator or a visual observer; a skier facing downhill cannot watch a glider behind them — no legal US solo operation without a waiver.
Resort written permission (gate for every concept); many resorts ban drones outright.
Landing at the lift approach (the most crowded spot) every run; no bystander detection in the landing logic beyond the rider.
Pusher prop near the hand at throw; snow strikes at 6–12 J.

consistencyChecks.finding: criteria.js says "no product artefact ≥1 px over the subject". kite2 tolerates a line/boom artefact up to 3 % of subject height (≈15 px at 520 px; boom stub ≈4.5 px wide over the rider in 100 % of filming frames → literal rule gives avail 0 %); towglider counts a frame bad only when ≥3 px of ≥1 px-wide leash lies over the subject; leapfrog has no tether (airframe occlusion only). The tolerances differ in kind and size.
consistencyChecks.favours: kite2 (avail passes only under its 3 % tolerance); towglider mildly

consistencyChecks.finding: FULLRUN_CASES has no wind between 3 and 6 m/s, where every tail gate sits. Auditor off-grid runs (same seeds): towglider tail3.5–4 → KE 21–22 J, headClear 0.36 m, ops 3 (audit3/towglider/out_tail_edge*.json); leapfrog launches in 4/15 band runs and is left behind → ops 3, avail 0–72 %, KE ≤14.303 J, headClear ≥1.97 m (safe but fails ops); kite2 robust: avail 72–82 %, KE ≤12.745 J, headClear ≥1.136 m, ops 1.
consistencyChecks.favours: towglider and leapfrog in grid-only tables

consistencyChecks.finding: Brief approximation (skier.pos + 1.75·0.92 m vertical) vs concept body-model head (includes carving lean). kite2 dev 1.105 m (body head) vs 0.17 m with the vertical approximation (boom/line pass near the vertical point when the rider leans 45°); towglider 1.011 (own) vs 0.859 (vertical, 9/39 runs <1.0); leapfrog 1.89 vs 1.88. Also: kite2 excludes the worn 1.2 m boom (passes 0.42 m from the helmet centre) because the definition covers only airborne parts.

env.footage() subjectPx is the full bounding box incl. ski tips, not feet→head as criteria.js words it. Strict feet→head: towglider avail 72 → 52 %, pxMed 535 → 373. Applies to every concept using env.footage (not re-run for kite2/leapfrog).

Round-2 oracle gates are removed: all three use windEstimate() for launch/park/no-fly gates. Remaining idealisations: kite2 tip-pitot/in-flight control on noise-free local wind; leapfrog in-flight estimate initialised with true wind and noise-free gust interlock; towglider estimate has no history at t=0.5 s (false refusal in 2 cross9 runs — penalises towglider).

All use enduranceMin(..., {heated}) with the heater over the whole day. Idle electronics on the lift are not charged by any concept; towglider most sensitive (57.8 → 39 min if the hip unit stays on). kite2 includes a winch-regeneration credit (48.5 min without).

Setup is simulated for all three; residual constants: kite2 2 s arm tap; leapfrog 8 s pick-up/fold and 2.5 s no-fly handling (≥13.5 s fold → p90 >30 s); towglider none found. Mass budgets: leapfrog 4 g NPU instead of the shared 11 g vision computer (172 g → avail 69.3 %, endurance 49.3 on a subset).

kite2: zero-lag heave-compensating winch beyond its own motor constants (needs 6–8 m/s reel-in, 93–166 W) and a boom gimbal sized for 0.13 N·m vs 0.35–1 N·m simulated load (passive boom → avail 42.9 %); towglider: 8 % EIS residual (15 % → jitter p90 2.99, 25 % → 4.65); leapfrog: perfect offline subject tracking (live framing 7.1, UWB-only pointing 4.2 °/s).
consistencyChecks.favours: each concept in its own table

consistencyChecks.finding: All three developer ensembles reproduce exactly from a copy of sim/ (max abs diff 0–0.002 on judged columns); auditor-own recomputations agree (towglider body force 5.3 vs 4.3 N, avail 72.01 vs 72.10 — immaterial).

ranking.question: usable solo follow-cam (self-operated, full run, real winds, minimal set-up)
ranking.summary: No concept is a usable solo follow-cam as specified. kite2 is the only one passing all 13 metrics as modelled (4 conditional) and is the most robust across winds incl. the off-grid tail band, but its pass rests on idealised actuators and a 3 % artefact tolerance, and the line/boom 0.8 m above snow behind the rider is an unfixed clothesline hazard. leapfrog and towglider fail the judged avail honestly (tail-wind refusals). Ranking is by credible usable envelope × evidence × safety, not by count of passes.

order.label: most credible light-wind follow-cam; fails all-weather avail
order.rationale: Reproduces exactly; fails only avail (75.2 %; flown 91.7 %, calm/cross 96–97 %) because it honestly refuses tailwinds ≥≈4.5 m/s estimated. KE 13.6 J (gate-bypass 13.4 J), headClear 1.88 m, no tether, ops p90 2. Conditions: perfect offline tracking for jitter (2.22 °/s), 8 s gloved fold, 2.72 L tight holster, 48.6 m vs 50 m C0 follow-me limit, 3.5–4.5 m/s tail band → launched and left behind (ops 3). Conventional technology, no line hazard.

order.label: only all-13 pass as modelled; highest upside, unproven actuators, unfixed clothesline
order.rationale: All 13 reproduced and pass (avail 81.5, jitter 1.66, setup 4.7 s, ops 1, F 28 N, KE 12.9 J, headClear 1.10, endurance 56.9, packVol 2.86), KE now robust to L/D/mass, robust in the 3.5–5.5 m/s tail band. But avail margin 1.5 pp rests on a 3 % artefact tolerance (literal ≥1 px rule → 0 %), an active 1.2 m boom whose gimbal is undersized for its simulated torque (passive → 42.9 %) and a zero-lag winch beyond its motor model (no heave comp → 79.7 %); L/D 0.6 → 73 %. Line/boom 0.80–0.82 m above snow 1–2 m behind the rider in 39/39 runs: resort permission unlikely. Would move to rank 1 if bench tests confirm boom/winch and a clothesline mitigation exists.

order.label: lowest burden but unsafe in the off-grid tail band; fails avail
order.rationale: ops 1, setup 12 s, 0.46 kg, 2.8 L (fold now geometrically consistent). Fails avail 72 % (6 tail runs refused, 2 cross9 false refusals). KE 14.0 and headClear 1.01 pass only at the grid winds: tail 3.5–4 m/s → 21–22 J and 0.36 m head pass; vertical-helmet headClear 0.86 m. Jitter rests on an 8 % EIS residual; endurance 39 min if lift idle is charged. Safety is the binding issue.

order.label: frozen negative result (round-2 row unchanged)
order.rationale: Round-2 audit: fails avail 29.6 %, setup 60 s, ops p90 3, KE 18 J, harmonised jitter p90 18 °/s. Not re-run in round 3.
